items.statement: Assuming AC_omega, for a boundaryless embedded Riemannian submanifold of a boundaryless ambient manifold, the following are equivalent: II=0; ambient covariant differentiation of tangent fields remains tangent; and every intrinsic affinely parametrized geodesic, on every common interval of definition, is an ambient affinely parametrized geodesic. AC_omega is inherited exactly through the smooth projections and geodesic existence.

items.title: Principal curvatures, Gaussian curvature, and mean curvature of an oriented hypersurface
items.statement: Assuming AC_omega, for a positive-dimensional hypersurface M^m with supplied smooth unit normal ν, the self-adjoint S_ν has an unordered multiset of real eigenvalues κ_1,…,κ_m. Define extrinsic Gaussian curvature det S_ν and scalar mean curvature (1/m)tr S_ν. Reversing ν negates every κ_i and the mean curvature, and multiplies det S by (-1)^m; AC_omega is inherited exactly through the shape-operator construction.

items.title: First variation of volume for a normal variation
items.statement: Assuming AC_omega, let F:(-ε,ε)×M→M̄ be a smooth family of immersions of a positive-dimensional m-manifold, with F_0=f and compactly supported variation field V normal along f. For every compact smooth domain K with supp V contained in its relative interior, define A_K(t)=∫_K μ_{F_t^*ḡ}; then A_K'(0)=-m∫_K⟨V,H_f⟩μ_g=-m∫_M⟨V,H_f⟩μ_g, independently of K. If M is compact, K=M gives total volume. When M is boundaryless the same formula holds for arbitrary compactly supported variations, because tangential variation is removed by reparametrization. AC_omega is inherited through normal projections and density integration.

items.title: Mean curvature and minimal submanifolds
items.statement: Assuming AC_omega, a positive-dimensional immersion with H_f=0 is called minimal and, when its source is boundaryless, is stationary for all compactly supported volume variations. The Clifford torus in S^3 shows minimal need not mean totally geodesic, and the equator's latitude variation shows stationary need not mean locally minimizing. Boundary-moving claims, regularity, existence, stability, and the wider minimal-surface theory are outside this page.
